title: FREE 4/5 days Gentleman split (part. 2)
summary: NH finishes the gentleman split with the optional Saturday arm day built from giant sets, then explains the blank template, which gives movement patterns and leaves exercise choice to the viewer. He warns against program hopping and against random exercise mixes that break the split's synergy.
claims: A good arm day includes compound movements; an arm day with none is a pro split, a bad arm day
Skew the arm day toward what you need; the requester needs shoulders so he gets shoulder work there
The arm day is the giant set day: small muscles have low cardiovascular demand so they are easier to superset, and you save time
Nothing is less taxing on the cardiovascular system than a curl, so never rest after curls; superset them
Giant set 1: hammer or supinated curls 8-12, standing DB overhead press 6-10, standing French press 6-10, seal rows 8-12
Schedule the equipment-heavy arm day early Saturday morning when the gym is empty
Well-done giant sets do not limit performance; seal rows still go fine after curls, press and French press
EZ bar preacher curl with a close grip, not going all the way down, is very good for the biceps; 8-12 to prevent ego lifting
Face pulls 15-20 since you do not go to failure on them; you just want quality reps
Giant set 2: preacher curls 8-12, cable lateral raises 10-15, face pulls 15-20, DB rows 8-12
Giant-setting the arm day cuts it from roughly four hours to about 1h15-1h30
Use 3-4 sets, or even 2-4, for arm day giant sets so you do not do useless sets after burning out; it is a learning curve
The arm day is optional because there is arm work elsewhere, but that is not sufficient past a certain point, which is why arm days matter
The rep ranges he gave the requester apply to everyone and can be copied into the blank template
The blank template is like a choose-your-own-adventure book: he did most of the work, you choose exercises and learn how programming works
The generic template includes a horizontal press on arm day because more bench volume is always good
Pick any exercise for each pattern (dip, seated press, Viking press), but keep choices specific so lifts feed each other; a random mix kills the split's synergy
Do not jump to every new program he publishes; stick with one and eventually make your own
exercises: close grip, don't go all the way down
